newsitem.title: USA: Japan must deregulate, open up markets - Eizenstat.
newsitem.headline: Japan must deregulate, open up markets - Eizenstat.

text.p: Japan needs to do more to open up its markets, U.S. State Department official Stuart Eizenstat said on Friday.
"They have to deregulate, they have to open up their economy, they have to reduce market barriers, otherwise they will restrict their own growth," Eizenstat told Reuters Financial Television.

Eizenstat, Undersecretary of State for Commercial and Business Affairs, criticized "byzantine" Japanese port regulations and noted that no "open skies" agreement had yet been reached to liberalize air transport markets. "These are the kinds of improvements...that need to be done," he said.

He said the United States was still examining what was meant by a Japanese commitment for "fully liberalized skies". Progress had been made on opening up the auto market, but there were still problems with new dealerships.
He said the United States was worried that the Japanese current account surplus was rising again after several years of decline.

"We had the good fortune in having a fairly substantial decline in their suplus in the last few years but there is no question...that that decline has stopped and the surplus is going up and this is going to put the Japan issue more on the front burner," he said. "We are concerned about it."
